narrative: OMX30 faces significant headwinds this morning despite maintaining +1.1% above its 200-day moving average. The global correlation signal is deeply negative at -1.064%, with Asian equities leading selloff (Nikkei -5.06%) and US tech collapsing (NASDAQ -2.39%) as the Jensen Huang rally exhausts. VIX has spiked to 29.06, reflecting elevated risk aversion. Technically, the index is in lower half of Bollinger Bands (%B=0.11) with RSI at 39.29 showing neutral-to-soft momentum, MACD below signal line, and critically weak ADX (14.4) which reduces forecast confidence to Low. Oil down 2.58% and copper crashed 3.82%, directly pressuring the 36% allocation to industrials and mining. Only mild support from USD/SEK (+0.08%) and defensive positioning offer relief.
morningBrief: OMX30 likely opens -0.4% to -0.6% on broad risk-off backdrop. Watch 3085 support (lower Bollinger) and 3123 (yesterday close) as key intraday pivots; 3180 (50-MA) is now resistance on oversold technics. ADX weakness (14.4) means reduced directional confidence—treat bounces with skepticism. Industrials (Atlas Copco, Volvo, Sandvik) face margin pressure from commodity rout; banks (SEB, Handelsbanken) gain minor NIM traction but sentiment overwhelms. Tech/telecom (Ericsson, Hexagon) follow NASDAQ lead lower. Pharma/defensive (AstraZeneca, Essity) hold relative strength. USD/SEK +0.08% offers thin exporter tailwind; monitor for renewed risk liquidation if US Jobless Claims (14:30 CET) surprise weak. Copper down 3.82% makes Boliden vulnerable despite gold holding—avoid chasing oversold bounces until VIX stabilizes below 25.
